title: Varying TTFT Across Deployments — Fanout & routing mitigation hotfix
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Over the last 36 hours multiple customers reported intermittent regressions in time-to-first-token (TTFT) and sustained tokens/sec across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments for several mid-sized decoder models (approx 6-13B). Symptoms varied by deployment: Hosted showed initial-token stalls on short prompts, Dedicated saw reduced sustained token throughput under burst, and Private deployments reported higher variance during model fanout. Initial alerts correlated with a canary rollout of a kernel-selection heuristic (KERNEL-OPT-2026-03) and a batching policy tweak that nudged prefetch timing.

Root cause hypothesis: The new kernel-selection heuristic caused a subset of worker pools to select a quantized int8 micro-kernel that performs poorly for short-sequence priming patterns. That choice, combined with more aggressive multiplex batching and a timing shift in KV-prefetch, created cold-path warmup churn and premature KV eviction on pooled hosts. The result: longer initial decode latency (first token) and lower tokens/sec until warm caches rebuilt.

Immediate mitigating actions taken: 
- Rolled back kernel-selection heuristic on canary and then regional pools (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1982).
- Introduced an emergency routing override to prefer warmed worker variants for customer tiers with SLA > 99.9% (feature toggle: routing.temp_prefer_warmed=true).
- Slowed KV-prefetch aggressiveness by adjusting prefetch_window from 120ms to 40ms for short sessions in hosted pools.
- Deployed a short-lived circuit breaker to cap the number of simultaneous fanout requests to vulnerable model families.

Planned next steps (this ticket): 
1) Stabilize and monitor the rollback effects across Hosted/Dedicated/Private for 48 hours.
2) Add a deterministic warmstart probe that fires a small priming request when a worker transitions to a quantized kernel path.
3) Instrument a new metric (kernel_selection_fail_rate) and add it to the Console SLO dashboard with alerts at 0.5% deviation.
4) Rework kernel-selection heuristic to prefer empirical micro-benchmark scores per sequence-length histogram rather than a single global ranking.
5) Postmortem with customer-facing RCA and recommended mitigations for private deployments (config knobs).

Relevant links:
- Live dashboard (token telemetry): https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/ttft-ledger?range=24h
- Incident runbook excerpt: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/TTFT+Regression+Runbook
